newsitem.title: CHINA: Extradited HK tobacco executive committed for trial.
newsitem.headline: Extradited HK tobacco executive committed for trial.

text.p: A former Hong Kong tobacco executive extradited from the United States to face bribery charges has been committed for trial, the territory's anti-corruption watchdog said.
Jerry Lui Kin-hong, 42, was remanded in custody after appearing in court on Wednesday, the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) said in a statement.
He was charged by the ICAC with nine offences including conspiracy and accepting bribes, and was committed to the Court of First Instance of the High Court for trial on a date to be fixed.

Lui is alleged to have accepted bribes of more than HK$31 million (US$4.0 million) in connection with a cigarette smuggling syndicate while he was a tobacco company executive in Hong Kong. He was arrested in Boston in 1995.

A Boston District Court in January blocked Lui's extradition after defence lawyers argued he faced possible execution if forced to return to Hong Kong, as his trial was unlikely to be completed before the territory's reversion to Chinese rule.
The decision caused a furore in Hong Kong and was seen as undermining efforts to persuade the world it would retain judicial independence after the handover.
A U.S. federal court in March ordered Lui's extradition and the Supreme Court in Washington later rejected his last application to appeal. He was flown to Hong Kong in May.
